title: Junctions: Emerging, Turning & Priorities
whatItIs: How to approach, turn at and emerge from junctions: who has priority, where to position, and the faults examiners record most often.

keyFacts.text: At a 'Stop' sign with a solid white line, you MUST stop behind the line, then wait for a safe gap.
At broken white lines across the road, you MUST give way to traffic on the main road.
You MUST NOT enter a yellow box until your exit is clear, unless turning right and held only by oncoming traffic.

keyFacts: Give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross the road you're turning into or out of.
Turning right: position just left of the middle of the road, wait for a safe gap and don't cut the corner.
Dual carriageway: wait in the central reservation only if it's deep enough to protect your whole vehicle.

visual.caption: Junction markings you MUST obey (Highway Code rules 171, 172, 174)

items.label: Stop line (with 'Stop' sign)
items.meaning: Stop behind the line, then go only when there is a safe gap.

items.label: Give way lines
items.meaning: Give way to traffic on the main road.

items.label: Yellow box junction
items.meaning: Don't enter until your exit is clear (except right turns held by oncoming traffic).

a.label: Right side to right side
points: Keep the other vehicle on your right and turn behind it
Generally safer: clear view of approaching traffic

b.label: Left side to left side
points: Turn in front of each other
Can block your view: cyclists and motorcyclists may be hidden
Layout, markings or the other vehicle may decide the method

onTheTest.question: Your pupil is turning left into a side road. A pedestrian is waiting to cross that side road. What should the pupil do?
options: Turn first: the pedestrian must wait
Sound the horn and continue the turn
onTheTest.why: Rule H2 and rule 170: at a junction, give way to pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road into which or from which you are turning. Beckoning pedestrians is recorded as a fault.

onTheTest.question: On test, a candidate looks before emerging but misjudges an approaching car, which has to slow down. Safety was not compromised. How does DT1 class this?
onTheTest.why: DT1 11.05 uses this example for a low-risk driving fault. Not taking effective observation and emerging into the path of other vehicles would be serious.

traps: A car from the right signalling left may not turn: wait and make sure before you emerge.
Approaching too slowly or waiting when it's safe to go is also a fault (undue hesitation), not just going too fast.
Traffic lights out of order? Treat it as an unmarked junction, where nobody has priority, and take great care.
Stay behind cyclists, horse riders and motorcyclists at junctions, even if they wait close to the kerb.
